Cisco IOS: Switch Configuration & VLAN Management

Cisco IOS (Internetwork Operating System) utilizes a hierarchical command structure. Mastering the transition between these modes is fundamental to switch administration.


1. IOS Command Hierarchy

The switch operates in several distinct modes, each with its own set of available commands.

PromptModePurpose
Switch>User EXECBasic monitoring and limited status checks.
Switch#Privileged EXECDetailed verification, administration, and saving configs.
Switch(config)#Global ConfigurationModifying settings that affect the entire switch.
Switch(config-if)#Interface ConfigurationConfiguring a specific physical port or SVI.
Switch(config-line)#Line ConfigurationConfiguring console or VTY (remote) access.

Navigation Flow: User EXEC -> enable -> Privileged EXEC -> configure terminal -> Global Config -> interface <id> -> Interface Config.


2. Base Hardening & Identity

Before deploying a switch, it must be secured to prevent unauthorized access and ensure clear identification.

Identity & Global Settings

  • Hostname: hostname S1 (Identifies the switch in logs and prompts).
  • DNS Suppression: no ip domain-lookup (Prevents the switch from hanging when a mistyped command is interpreted as a DNS query).
  • MOTD Banner: banner motd #Authorized users only# (Displays legal warnings at login).

Access Control

  • Privileged Mode: enable secret class (Protects the transition to Privileged EXEC).
  • Console Access: 
    line console 0
password cisco
login
exit
  • Remote Access (VTY): 
    line vty 0 4
password cisco
login
transport input telnet
exit
  • Password Obfuscation: service password-encryption (Encrypts plain-text passwords in the configuration file).

3. Port Security (The Edge Defense)

Port security restricts input to an interface by limiting the MAC addresses allowed to send traffic.

Sticky MACs: The `switchport port-security mac-address sticky` command allows the switch to dynamically learn a MAC address and automatically add it to the running configuration, ensuring the device remains authorized after a reboot.

Configuration Workflow:

interface fastEthernet 0/1
 switchport mode access
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 2
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky
 switchport port-security violation protect
 no shutdown

Violation Modes:

  • Protect: Drops unauthorized traffic without notifying the admin or shutting the port.
  • Restrict: Drops traffic and logs the violation.
  • Shutdown: Immediately disables the port (err-disable state).

4. VLANs & Logical Segmentation

Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) allow a physical switch to be partitioned into multiple logical broadcast domains.

VLAN Creation & Assignment

  1. Define the VLAN: vlan 10 -> name Enseignant
  2. Assign an Access Port: interface fastEthernet 0/3 -> switchport mode access -> switchport access vlan 10

SVIs (Switched Virtual Interfaces)

An SVI is a logical interface that represents a VLAN. It is primarily used for switch management (SSH/Telnet).

interface vlan 99
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown

Trunking (802.1Q)

Trunks allow a single physical link to carry traffic for multiple VLANs between switches.

interface fastEthernet 0/8
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,99

5. VTP (VLAN Trunking Protocol)

VTP synchronizes VLAN databases across switches in the same domain, reducing manual configuration overhead.

ModeRoleBehavior
ServerAdministratorCan create/modify/delete VLANs; propagates changes to clients.
ClientReceiverReceives VLAN updates; cannot modify the VLAN database.
TransparentIndependentForwards VTP updates but maintains its own local VLAN database.

Basic Setup: vtp domain <name> -> vtp mode <server/client> -> vtp password <pass>


📊 Operator’s Verification Cheat Sheet

CommandVerification Goal
show running-configCurrent active configuration in RAM.
show startup-configConfiguration saved to NVRAM.
show vlan briefPort-to-VLAN assignments and VLAN status.
show interfaces trunkTrunking status and allowed VLAN list.
show ip interface briefIP addresses and operational state of SVIs.
show port-securityGlobal port security status.
show vtp statusVTP domain, mode, and revision number.
copy running-config startup-configSaves the active configuration to persist after reboot.
